name: Lagoon
notes: Sheltered coastal lagoons: mangroves and sea purslane on tropical lagoon shores, samphire/saltwort and reeds on temperate barrier lagoons (Venice, Baltic haffs), and dense seagrass meadows in the shallow water. Drawn on Caribbean and Indo-Pacific atoll lagoons, Mediterranean and Baltic lagoons; underwater species flagged.

traits.native_range: Avicennia germinans, Caribbean, Gulf of Mexico and W African lagoon shores, pneumatophore mats, 3-15 m — Wikipedia
traits.trunk: prop roots or pneumatophores over mud
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

bark.note: dark grey to black, fissured into small scaly plates; inner bark orange

canopy.silhouette: dark rounded mangrove dome above spiky pneumatophores

growth.juvenile_note: Cryptoviviparous: the embryo germinates inside the fruit on the tree. A stranded propagule sheds its skin, opens two thick, folded, fleshy green cotyledons like a butterfly and anchors with a hairy radicle. The seedling is a slender single stem with opposite, leathery, narrow leaves, grey-hairy beneath; pencil-like pneumatophores soon ring the young tree.
growth.source: USDA Tropical Tree Seed Manual, Avicennia germinans (14-20 m, young trees add ~60 cm/yr, viviparous, propagules float >4 months); Useful Tropical Plants (seedlings 26 cm at 4 months); first flowering age and lifespan estimated.

fruiting.source: USDA Tropical Tree Seed Manual (flowers May-Jul, white with yellow base, nectar-rich honey flowers, flattened 2-valved capsule, propagules peak Sep-Oct); Useful Tropical Plants (cotyledons eaten in famine after careful preparation); flower life, fruit set and crop estimated.

growth.juvenile_note: The husked nut lies on the sand and after 2-6 months a pointed shoot pushes out of one end while the nut's flesh feeds the seedling. First leaves are entire, stiff, strap-like blades split only at the tip (bifid), in a stemless fan-like rosette; pinnate fronds come later, and a trunk rises after ~3-5 years, widening from a bulbous base ('bole').
growth.source: Wikipedia Coconut (tall palms bear at 6-10 yr, live 60-100 yr; ~11 months from female flower opening to harvest; up to 15 inflorescences/yr; ~80 nuts/yr, up to 150; nut ~1.4 kg; largely cross-pollinated, dwarfs selfing); ICRAF Agroforestree (tall selections 24-30 m, flowers after ~6th yr); germination from FAO coconut guides

fruiting.source: Wikipedia Coconut and ICRAF (new inflorescence among the leaves every ~3-4 weeks, up to 15/yr, thousands of small male flowers and ~20-50 large 25 mm female flowers per inflorescence; cross-pollinated by insects and wind; ~11-12 months to a mature brown nut that drops; 50-150 nuts per palm per year)

growth.juvenile_note: Viviparous: the seed sprouts on the tree and a green, pencil-like hypocotyl 20-30 cm long hangs from the brown fruit. It drops, floats (weeks, up to a year), lodges upright in mud, roots from the lower tip within days and opens a pair of glossy leaves at the top. The sapling is a single stem that soon throws down arching red-brown prop roots.
growth.source: Tropical Plants Database (theferns.info) Rhizophora mangle (1-1.5 m/yr on productive sites; 5-20 m, rarely 30; flowers year-round; flowering by 6 yr, even 3-5 yr at 0.5-1 m tall; propagules 8-30 cm); Wikipedia (to 24 m, commonly ~6 m; propagules may float over a year); lifespan and shade estimated

fruiting.source: Tropical Plants Database (flowers all year; bees and wind; 4-7 months from fertilization to hypocotyl emergence plus 4-6 months more before it falls; propagules 8-30 cm); Wikipedia (pale yellow flowers; self or wind pollination); fruit size given for the hanging propagule; set, crop and decay estimated

growth.juvenile_note: Seeds sprout within a day on wet mud; seedlings are tiny, with two small cotyledons and thread-thin shoots set with minute scale leaves, growing a few mm a day. They branch from the base into a feathery, multi-stemmed shrub of slender purplish-brown stems and blue-green scale-leaved sprays, later a small gnarled tree.
growth.source: Wikipedia Tamarix gallica (to ~5 m; pink flowers in narrow feathery spikes, first in May and sometimes again in August); USDA FEIS Tamarix spp. incl. French tamarisk (germination <24 h, seedlings 2-5 mm/day, flowering from year 1-3, resprouts 3-4 m in a season). Height-age curve and lifespan estimated.

fruiting.source: Wikipedia (tiny pink flowers in feathery spikes, May and again in August); USDA FEIS Tamarix spp. (5-merous flowers, insect cross-pollinated, ~20 flowers per 2.5 cm of raceme, 8-20+ tiny plumed seeds per capsule). Flower life, fruit set, ripening and crop estimated.

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling with 2 oval cotyledons, then fleshy, glossy, bright-green spoon-shaped leaves crowded in a tuft at the shoot tip. fruiting.source: Wikipedia Scaevola taccada: flowers all year in small axillary clusters, white 'half flowers' 2-2.5 cm with the 5 petal lobes fanned to one side, sometimes violet-streaked, pollinated by large bees or selfed; round fleshy drupe ripening green to white, corky stone floats in seawater; ripening time, set and crop estimated

growth.juvenile_note: The tiny corky two-winged fruits float on the tide and sprout on wet sand or marl above the mangroves. Seedlings carry small leathery lance-shaped leaves (silvery-hairy in the silver form) and soon branch from the base into a bushy, often leaning, multi-stemmed shrub that ages into a gnarled, twisted small tree; broken branches root readily.
growth.source: Useful Tropical Plants (theferns.info: 4-20 m, medium growth, full sun, sow fresh seed, large cuttings root); Wikipedia (multi-trunked shrub 1-4 m to tree 20 m); FNPS (long-lived, flowers/fruits all year); ResearchGate buttonwood germination study (germination peaking in week 2)

fruiting.source: Wikipedia (button-like heads 5-8 mm, 35-56 flowers, red-brown cone-like fruit heads 5-15 mm that burst when ripe, water-dispersed); FNPS (flowers and fruits all year, bee and hairstreak nectar plant). Fruit set, ripening time and crop estimated.

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal seedling with two fleshy, strap-like cotyledons, then small, fleshy, half-round blue-green leaves crowded along a thin stem. It hardens into a woody-based, densely branched evergreen bush of glaucous succulent leaves, often forming low hummocks on shingle at the top of salt marshes; leaves may redden in winter.
growth.source: Wikipedia Suaeda vera (small shrub of arid salt flats and salt marshes; in Britain mainly where shingle meets salt marsh; seeds germinate more readily in fresh than in salt water). Stature (to ~1.2 m), growth rate, age at first flowering and lifespan estimated from shrubby halophytes.

fruiting.source: British flora accounts (tiny green petal-less flowers 1-3 in the leaf axils, Jul-Oct; fruit a utricle in the persistent fleshy perianth with one shiny black seed ~1-1.5 mm). Pollination, ripening, persistence and crop estimated from Suaeda biology.

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings are small, weak, grass-like tufts of soft green leaves on wet mud. After a season rhizomes and long surface runners spread out; every spring new culms shoot up like thin canes to full height in a few months, with long, broad, grey-green leaves all along the stem and a big, silky, purple-brown plume that fades to grey-buff.
growth.source: USDA FEIS Phragmites australis (germination needs light, moisture and warm alternating temperatures after cold stratification; seedling survival very low; 3-4 years to viable seed; maximum height at 5-8 years; no part of a clone lives more than 8 years though clones persist far longer; culms die back yearly)

growth.juvenile_note: A 2 mm seed germinates on sandy mud of the middle shore; the seedling is a tiny tuft of 2-3 thread-narrow, dark green, blunt leaves with a few fine roots. It soon sends out a thin creeping rhizome that branches and roots at each node, with a tuft of 2-5 short strap leaves at every node, knitting into a flat green turf that lies limp on the mud at low tide.
growth.source: Wikipedia (Zostera noltei): leaves to 22 cm in groups of 2-5, up to 4 roots per node, seeds about 2 mm; grows in spring, flowers in dense summer beds, loses most leaves over winter; rhizome clumps may live many years; intertidal, harmed by nutrients and turbid water. Germination, shoot life and flowering age estimated.

growth.juvenile_note: The floating 'sea olive' splits and drops its seed, which germinates at once: a small white root, then a tuft of 3-6 short, bright green strap leaves from the stout seed, anchored by hairy roots in sand or rock crevices. A new leaf appears only about every 51 days and the rhizome creeps just 1-6 cm a year, so a patch spreads extremely slowly.
growth.source: Wikipedia (leaves to 1-1.5 m x 1 cm; horizontal rhizome 1-6 cm/yr, vertical 0.1-4 cm/yr; a new leaf about every 51 days; flowers Sept-Oct, fruit matures in about 6 months; an Ibiza clone ~8 km across is estimated at 100,000 yr). Shoot lifespan, time to full leaf length and first flowering (rare, episodic) estimated.

growth.juvenile_note: Seeds have no dormancy and sprout within days of release from the big ribbed fruit, often while drifting. The seedling is a small fan of a few short, flat, ribbon-like leaves from a stout rhizome; it anchors with thick cord-like roots and grows into a tall shoot of long, strap-like leaves (to 1.5 m) sheathed at the base in black fibrous remains of old leaves.
growth.source: Wikipedia Enhalus acoroides (leaves 30-150 cm; rhizomes ~1.5 cm thick; the only surface-pollinated seagrass, male flowers detach and float; fruit round, 4-6 cm, dark and ribbed, with 6-7 white seeds; to ~4 m deep on mud, sand and coral flats). Seed germination speed, growth and shoot lifespan estimated from seagrass literature.
